messages.author: 4184023bb084c468
messages.subject: using knitr-generated markdown in nanoc
parts:
Hi,

I am generating markdown files from .Rmd documents using knitr, and then I want to feed those markdown files to nanoc (http://nanoc.ws/) which will create HTML pages from them which will have the look and feel of other pages on my website (this is why I don't go directly from .Rmd to HTML in knitr).

Nanoc does not seem to understand syntax like this:

```r
# some code
```

I want this to be rendered like code:

<pre><code># some code</code></pre>

But it ends up being rendered by nanoc like this:

<p><code>r
# some code
</code></p>

There are two problems with that; the first is, I don't want the 'r' to be visible.
Secondly, without the <pre>, the code looks wrong.

Nanoc thinks it's inline code, I guess, the kind you would use if you just wanted to call out a single word as code within a line of text.

So I'm not sure if this is a knitr or a nanoc question--I'll ask a similar question in the nanoc discussion group. 
But is knitr producing some extension of pure markdown? Github-flavored markdown? Can it be made to produce 'pure' markdown instead?

Or alternatively, is there a way to write my Rmd documents in a 'purer' markdown and still have the code chunks evaluated (unless I specify otherwise)?

Thanks,
Dan

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] using knitr-generated markdown in nanoc
parts:
Hi Dan,

You can use 

    render_markdown(strict=TRUE)

before calling knitr to get 'pure' markdown output.

Like you surmise  the ```r is Github-flavored markdown (also recognized by pandoc, sundown (the rstudio parser), maybe others) as a code block in the r language (for highlighting).  

- Carl

messages.author: c91a208fffacfb7e
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] using knitr-generated markdown in nanoc
parts:
The convention of
```r
# some code
```
using the syntax highlighting for the R language was introduced in github-flavored markdown (see the "Syntax Highlighting" section of https://help.github.com/articles/github-flavored-markdown )  not the original markdown.  It is likely that nanoc was built on the original markdown syntax.
